key_insight: An autonomous AI workflow identified perovskite compositions with high predicted hydrogen production capacity for chemical looping, rather than solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Combining hydrogen capacity with raw-material price, supply resilience, and potential environmental and health impacts helps prioritize candidates for practical deployment.
method: Combine a Wasserstein autoencoder with a deep ensemble surrogate in an active-learning loop.
Search perovskite compositions for high hydrogen production capacity.
Use multi-objective ranking to select 20 diverse candidates.
evidence_signal: Across seven independent 50-cycle runs, mean acquired hydrogen capacity rose from 0.41 to 2.05 mmol H₂/g, with best compositions reaching 2.65–2.99 mmol H₂/g.
watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental validation or long-term redox cycling stability, both essential before deployment.
paper_title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
